content.value_statement: Platform reports can overstate conversions when several channels claim the same order. This skill matches conversion exports to an order-ID truth set and produces a normalized reconciliation view.
actual_capabilities: Matches platform-reported conversions to GA4 or ecommerce order IDs.
Separates matched, double-counted, and unmatched conversion claims.
Normalizes attribution windows and monetary values to a stated common basis.
Compares credit allocation across at least two attribution models.
Reads geo or holdout results when a suitable export is supplied.
Prepares de-duplicated counts for a separate ROI and ROAS calculation.
limitations: Requires a GA4 or ecommerce order-ID export as the truth set.
Uses only the accuracy and completeness of the exports supplied.
Cannot infer incrementality without a geo or holdout test export.
Does not calculate ROAS, CPA, ROI, or other ratio metrics.

use_cases.title: Audit overlapping platform claims
use_cases.description: Compare Meta and Google conversion exports with a GA4 order export to identify sales claimed by multiple platforms.

use_cases.title: Build a monthly reconciliation
use_cases.description: Create a recurring workbook that tracks matched, double-counted, and unmatched conversions across paid channels.

use_cases.title: Interpret a holdout test
use_cases.description: Compare test and control order exports with platform spend to distinguish measured lift from last-click credit.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic reconciliation
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile these Meta and Google conversion exports against this GA4 order-ID export for May. Show matched, double-counted, and unmatched orders.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize platform reporting
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a monthly attribution reconciliation. Normalize Meta 7-day-click and Google 30-day windows to the order dates, then state the currency basis used.

prompt_templates.title: Compare credit allocation
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this reconciled order set, compare last-click and linear attribution by platform. Keep the total number of real orders unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Read a geo holdout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these test-region and control-region order exports and spend data to assess incrementality. Compare measured lift with last-click claims and mark unsupported conclusions.

output_examples.input: Meta, Google, and GA4 order exports for one month.
output: A match table for every platform claim.
A list of unmatched claims that need investigation.

output_examples.input: A test and control regional order export with spend data.
output: A stated estimate of measured lift or an explanation of missing inputs.
A comparison between holdout evidence and attributed conversions.
A note that ROAS and CPA require a separate calculation.

best_practices: Provide complete order IDs, timestamps, values, currencies, and attribution windows for every export.
Use the ecommerce or GA4 order export as the truth set, not platform-reported totals.
Review unmatched claims before using reconciled counts in budget decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not add platform conversion totals together without checking overlapping order IDs.
Do not compare counts from different attribution windows or currencies without normalization.
Do not claim incrementality when no valid geo or holdout evidence exists.

faq.question: What data do I need?
faq.answer: Provide a GA4 or ecommerce order-ID export and conversion exports from each paid platform. Include attribution windows and currencies.

faq.question: Can it reconcile Meta and Google data?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to identify orders claimed by multiple paid platforms.

faq.question: What is the truth set?
faq.answer: The truth set is the GA4 or ecommerce order-ID export. Platform conversion counts are claims to reconcile against it.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROAS or CPA?
faq.answer: No. It prepares de-duplicated counts for a separate ROI and ROAS calculation skill or workflow.

faq.question: Can it measure incrementality?
faq.answer: It can interpret supplied geo or holdout exports. It marks incrementality unavailable when no such evidence exists.

faq.question: Will it save my results?
faq.answer: It asks before saving a workbook for later sessions. Avoid saving unnecessary order-level data and follow your retention policy.
